summary: Catalog policy re-emission: pass slots published before the re_entry ride-along never reach access
description:
TKT-87 ai-review incidental (gpt-5.6-sol arm, G1). A slot published before the re_entry field existed has retained publication events without the field; access's projector writes explicit single and the publish path never re-emits an acknowledged publication. Any pre-existing multi/count_limited slot therefore enforces single forever, with no operator signal. Needs a catalog re-emission or backfill path (the projection's upsert already converges on a new envelope id) — the residual gap the TKT-87 plan named. Constraints: ADR-017 (any payload/schema decision), deterministic publication event ids (events.go EventID).

COS:
1. A multi/count_limited slot published before the re_entry ride-along enforces its real policy at the gate after the backfill/re-emission runs (proven end-to-end: catalog emit -> access projection -> scan).
2. The mechanism is idempotent and bounded: re-running it is a no-op (access side converges by envelope id; stream does not accumulate unbounded duplicates).
3. Inventory's consumption of the subject is provably unaffected (no duplicate pool provisioning; test evidence, not assertion).
4. Single-policy slots re-emit harmlessly.
5. make check green; ADR-017 discipline for any payload/schema decision.

governingAdrs.why: Whether a re-emission event rides the existing subject/schema or needs its own; consumer dispatch rules.
The policy being distributed; catalog owns it.

objective.note: Pass slots published before the re_entry ride-along project as single forever; catalog needs a re-emission/backfill path so access's projection converges.

scope.note: IN: catalog-side mechanism to (re)emit policy for already-published slots + access convergence proof. OUT: policy mutation/update API (still none), projector changes (upsert convergence already shipped in TKT-87).

uncertainties.note: Mechanism choice — one-shot backfill subcommand re-emitting publications with fresh envelope ids vs a dedicated policy event — is Planning's; ADR-017 fences it and the projector accepts either via new-envelope convergence. Trap to respect: publication event ids are deterministic (EventID = id+published_at), so a re-emission must NOT reuse them or JetStream/consumed_events dedup will swallow it.

dependencies.note: TKT-87 merged (projector + UpsertSlotPolicy convergence on new envelope ids). No open blockers.

approach.note: Leading option: catalog `publish-admission-policies`-style one-shot subcommand enumerating published slots and re-emitting at current schema with a distinct deterministic id; access needs zero changes.

first_slice.note: A multi slot published pre-TKT-87 gets its policy row in access after the backfill runs; single slots re-emit harmlessly (idempotent upsert).

success.note: COS on description: backfill idempotent + bounded; pre-existing pass slot enforces its real policy after run; no duplicate provisioning side-effects in inventory (same-id dedup or ignored fields — must be proven, inventory consumes this subject).
